questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Heritage, language practice, academic opportunities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy. I had severe communication issues with the recieving institution in the weeks leading up to the exchange as well as the first couple of weeks, leading to me missing the first weeks of courses as well as having to stay at a hotel, since my acommodation was blocked due to recieving institution forgetting to forward my information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a welcome day on the 6th of september, which was very informative. Sadly, any information before this date was very sparse, and it led me to miss courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
In more detail:
The recieving institution explicitly asked not to recieve any e-mails in july and august, as any issues would be solved in late august/early september due to vacation scheduling. I was granted a CROUS accomodation, that was organized through the university. For this I am very grateful. However, in the weeks leading up to my travels and move-in date, I recieved no information about my room. I tried reaching out to recieving institution to solve this, but getting no responses, I decided to show up at my logement, and found out that the university had forgotten to forward my information, almost resulting in me losing my room. 

In the end I had to stay five days in a hotel, as I could not access my room before the university forwarded my information, and it was impossible to reach anyone from the university. I tried showing up on september 1st at the faculty to actually speak with someone, but to my surprise, the office was exeptionally closed on this date. Moreover, I had many issues recieving my academic schedule resulting in me missing the first couple of weeks of courses. This made the time leading up to my exchange very stressful, the first weeks very frustrating, and the following weeks quite stressed as I had to catch up on a lot academically from the very start. 

I have spoken with several exchange students, who faced the same or similar issues as me.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy as it was organized through the university. Had there not been communication issues, it would have been very good!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very difficult to find anything in Strasbourg if you are staying for less than 6 months or have a french bank account, sadly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My host institution had someone manually registering us, making mistakes possible (and common) and also not making it very clear whether or not registering the courses would be possible.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You would send your learning agreement to the administrative office, who would then inscribe you. Once you did this, you had to make your own timetable, and just assume that inscription was possible. Sometimes courses were not visible on the timetable, so you would have to contact the admin office to fix this problem.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a dedicated person working with all the exchange students. He was extremely helpful but also very busy.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had to change one course as it was not available in the period I had chosen.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Assume that you are getting the courses you choose, don't wait for a confirmation.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one first year BA course, four third year BA courses and one 2nd year master course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style varied from course to course but in general it reminded me more of high school in Denmark in the sense that the teacher does role call and you are expected to show up unless you have a doctor's note that your are ill.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Économie Industrièlle
Jeux et Stratégies
Advanced Programming and Data Visualization
Histoire des concepts économiques 1
Economics and Business Management
Theory of Knowledge

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you haven't had Videnskabsteori yet, I recommend taking Theory of Knowledge. Économie Industrièlle and Jeux et Stratégies were both very micro-oriented and in a similar style to UCPH with a lot of exercises.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Because I lived in a CROUS, I had to buy pillows, towels, bedding, plates, cups, pot, pan etc. There was nothing when I arrived.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Don't buy insurance from home! You can buy way cheaper insurance for students in France! I did this mistake, and since my insurance policy was in danish, my logement did not accept it, so I had to buy another insurance.
Also, I did extra french classes which cost me 250 euros + an exam that cost 40 euros.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Unisport is great! Sign up in advance, but you can always try to show up for a class, even if you haven't signed up. Usually they have room on the day.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many I can't list them. Look into ESN and AESES for a start.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ESN had many great activities for meeting new people. Unisport was also great for the same reason.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around. Get a carte fluo, take the train to the villages in alsace, go hiking.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I was surprised at how social everyone were. In the first conversation it is normal to ask for someones contact info and also to go to activities together.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Everything is closed on sundays. Even supermarkets. During lunch a lot of things are closed as well.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Politeness and acknowledging even strangers' presence. Everyone holds the door for everyone.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: If you don't get an answer to an important e-mail within a couple of days, write again, insist, show up at their offices.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are a BA student in economics, you need to know french. At least B1, B2 preferrably. Exams are all written in hand.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social connections with both locals and other international students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Logistics. Before and during the exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
